findings.claim: The blob copy now spawns two git processes per file (laneGit runs `config --show-scope` before every `cat-file blob`), serially for each persona, and the reviewers' turn was already measured at :422 before this loop. On this repo (1455 files) with 3 to 5 personas that is several thousand spawns, tens of seconds up to minutes, with no total deadline (each call has its own 120 s), none of it counted against the turn or the loop's budget: the reviewers then still get the full turn, so the attempt overruns the time `left()` allowed, where `git archive` was one process per reviewer.
findings.fix: Build ONE copy per attempt with a single `cat-file --batch` (oids on stdin) and give each reviewer a clone of it (clonefile/cp -c), and measure `turn()` after the snapshots, returning budgetOut when it falls under reviewMinTurn.

findings.claim: When ~/.claude.json changed during the review, the outcome is replaced by silent even when the personas gave a confirmed veto, so an orphan of the judged agent that touches ~/.claude.json mid-review erases the only teeth the review has and the vetoed task passes; the spec says a global-config change does not fail the attempt 'por si', not that it cancels a veto, and a veto from a possibly tampered context can only fail more (the safe direction).
findings.fix: In the globalTouched branch keep `ran.outcome` when it is a veto (`!approved`) and only turn the non-veto outcome into `silent`, adding the config note to the veto's note.

findings.claim: The 64 MiB cap applies to every laneGit call (worktree, lane integration, diff), not only to the reviewer's `cat-file blob`, and BoundedProcess keeps both stdoutData and the decoded stdout String, so one big blob or diff holds about 128 MiB in the daemon per call where 1 MiB was the bound before.
findings.fix: Keep the 1 MiB default in laneGit and pass the 64 MiB cap only from reviewSnapshot (a laneGit overload with `cap:`), or stream the blob to the file instead of buffering it.

findings.claim: With A1 attempt 1 now passes (mute is no opinion), so attempt 2 never runs and the test can no longer fail if U1 regresses to a per-attempt base: the property it was written for (the next attempt still mute because the base is the loop's) is untested.
findings.fix: Make attempt 1 fail by its check (or by a veto) after planting the env, so attempt 2 runs and the test asserts its reviewers are mute with reviewGlobalConfigRiskyNote.

findings.claim: The ls-tree output is read as a String, so a path with non-UTF-8 bytes becomes U+FFFD and is written under another name (two such paths collide on O_EXCL and mute the reviewer); harmless under the parecer model, only a wrong copy or a 'sem parecer'.
findings.fix: Split `ls.stdoutData` on NUL bytes and build the path with the raw bytes (fileSystemRepresentation), or fail the copy explicitly on a non-UTF-8 path.

matrix: Checked and right: valid reject with a located blocker/major vetoes (review set, reviewRejects +1, twiceRefused on the 2nd in a row); reject with only minor/nit or an unlocated blocker, approve, approve with blocker (invalid), mute, invalid, all mute, no personas and configSilenced are notes and the attempt goes as the check and the gate decided; reviewBudgetOut uncounts and stops the loop; reviewerTouched with the tree changed fails as a move, not counted; ~/.claude.json changed alone is silent. Review runs only when AttemptDecision.reason is nil, so nothing passes that the check or the gate would fail, and without --review the machine never reaches reviewing. Reports and notes say 'parecer' (veto / sem veto / sem parecer / falhou), never 'aprovado'. GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS and core.commitGraph=false only change which objects are read and how fast, no worktree, lane, diff or patch command depends on either; 120000 becomes a text file, 160000 is skipped, a blob over the cap mutes that reviewer.

previous.claim: The agent-config check covered only reviewRoot itself and nothing refused a review in open mode (WorkLoopReview.swift:60).
previous.why: plantedConfig (Z2) now walks reviewRoot and every ancestor up to /, the home and ~/.claude/{CLAUDE.md,settings.json}; open mode is still not enforced in code (only the help says 'exige agentes em strict'), but under A1 a planted config can at most make a reviewer approve, which releases nothing, or mute it, which is 'sem parecer'.

previous.claim: The measured turn was compared only with 0, not with reviewMinTurn, so a short rest made every reviewer mute and counted as a refusal (WorkLoopReview.swift:172).
previous.why: review() now returns budgetOut when turn < min(reviewMinTurn, loop.timeout) (Z3a), and under A1 mute is no refusal anyway; the snapshot time after that measurement is the new major at :439.

previous.claim: On a touched tree, git clean -X deleted every ignored path that appeared during the review (WorkLoop.swift:552).
previous.why: reviewerLeftovers (Z3a) splits the fresh ignored paths: only agent configs are cleaned, with --literal-pathspecs, and the rest is kept and named in the note.

previous.claim: reviewTree's --ignored=matching with -unormal cannot see a new file inside an already ignored or untracked directory (WorkLoop.swift:941).
previous.why: reviewTree still runs status --ignored=matching without --untracked-files=all; Z3b's reviewHashAgentConfig covers the agent configs inside such folders, so it stays defense in depth (nit).
